title: Targeted Synthetic Falsification Corpus — Narrow Epistemic Join Clarification
controlling_law: NO SEMANTIC JOIN WITHOUT A WARRANT.

cases.title: Multiple partial sources with no synthesis method
cases.setup: Three synthetic sources each offer partial support for relation R. No declared inferential method combines them.
cases.expected: The sources may be compared, but no composite warrant exists and R remains CANDIDATE / UNESTABLISHED.
cases.failure: R becomes warranted solely from source count, compatibility, or apparent convergence.
cases.reason: ACT 11A requires a separately authored composite inference with an explicit composition method before a composite warrant candidate exists.

cases.title: Multiple partial sources with explicit governed triangulation method
cases.setup: Three synthetic sources provide complementary partial evidence. A separately authored triangulation analysis declares its proposition, support set, method, independence assumptions, jurisdiction, uncertainty, boundaries, and licensed semantics.
cases.expected: A new COMPOSITE WARRANT CANDIDATE may be evaluated on its own merits. It may earn only the standing justified by its method and support.
cases.failure: The analysis is either automatically promoted because multiple sources agree, or prohibited merely because no single source independently warrants R.
cases.reason: ACT 11A distinguishes the support set from the separately governed composite inference and explicitly preserves legitimate triangulation viability.

cases.title: Prestigious-source accumulation masquerading as warrant
cases.setup: Four highly prestigious synthetic authorities endorse nearby endpoint propositions, but none establishes relation R and no composite method exists.
cases.expected: Prestige does not create a warrant. R remains unestablished.
cases.failure: Authority prestige or agreement is aggregated into relation standing.
cases.reason: ACT 11A explicitly forbids source prestige, agreement, repetition, and count from substituting for a governed composite inference.

cases.title: Composite warrant with unresolved source dependence
cases.setup: A composite analysis combines three sources, but two may derive from the same undisclosed upstream dataset. The dependence cannot currently be resolved.
cases.expected: The dependence uncertainty must remain operative and cap standing; the sources may not be treated as independent.
cases.failure: The composite is evaluated as though the three sources were independent.
cases.reason: ACT 11A requires dependence assumptions and makes unresolved dependence part of the standing ceiling.

cases.title: Composite method licenses correlation but not causation
cases.setup: A separately governed composite method validly combines synthetic observational sources and supports an association between A and B, but contains no causal identification.
cases.expected: The composite warrant may support ASSOCIATION only; the causal proposition remains unestablished.
cases.failure: The composite warrant's standing is semantically strengthened from association to causation.
cases.reason: ACT 11A requires the relation semantics actually licensed by the composition method to remain explicit.

cases.title: Member adoption of personal meaning only
cases.setup: MAIA proposes that a synthetic member's recurring image may represent a desire for rest. The member says, 'Yes, that is what it means to me.'
cases.expected: Member-confirmed standing may be created for the personal-meaning component, with MAIA proposal provenance preserved.
cases.failure: The member is prevented from adopting their own meaning, or the original MAIA proposal provenance is erased.
cases.reason: ACT 11A preserves strong member authority over lived experience and personal meaning while retaining proposal/adoption history.

cases.title: Member adoption of mixed proposition containing another person's motive
cases.setup: MAIA proposes: 'Your partner's silence feels withholding because they intended to control you.' The member replies, 'Yes, exactly.'
cases.expected: The member may confirm that the silence feels withholding or controlling to them. The partner's motive/intention remains separately unwarranted.
cases.failure: Whole-sentence confirmation promotes the partner's hidden motive or intention to fact.
cases.reason: ACT 11A requires mixed components to retain distinct standing and keeps external motive claims independently warranted.

cases.title: Member confirms only part of a MAIA hypothesis
cases.setup: MAIA proposes two linked claims: 'This transition feels like grief, and it is caused by an unconscious archetypal mechanism.' The member confirms only, 'Yes, it feels like grief.'
cases.expected: Only the lived-experience component becomes member-confirmed. The causal/metaphysical component retains its previous standing and authorship.
cases.failure: Partial confirmation is treated as adoption of the entire proposition.
cases.reason: ACT 11A requires the actually adopted semantic components to remain recoverable and separately scoped.

cases.title: Practitioner interpretation later adopted by member
cases.setup: A synthetic practitioner says a recurring pattern may reflect unresolved fear and also asserts an external causal explanation. The member later says the 'unresolved fear' framing resonates.
cases.expected: Personal resonance may become member-confirmed; practitioner authorship remains recoverable; the external causal claim does not become member-authored fact.
cases.failure: Member resonance retroactively rewrites the entire practitioner proposition as member-authored truth.
cases.reason: ACT 11A expressly preserves practitioner provenance and separate warrant requirements for external factual/causal components.

cases.title: Mixed proposition requires different standing across semantic components
cases.setup: A single synthetic sentence combines: member feeling, personal interpretation, another person's motive, and a scientific generalization.
cases.expected: The proposition must remain decomposable conceptually so each component can carry its own authorship, jurisdiction, warrant, and standing.
cases.failure: The contract forces the entire sentence into one undifferentiated standing.
cases.reason: ACT 11A establishes a conceptual mixed-proposition rule without requiring a particular parser, schema, or implementation mechanism.
